title: Credential & Route Forensics Canvas (UX notes and triage flow)
summary: Sketch + interaction notes for a 'forensics canvas' view aimed at rapid triage of quota and throttle incidents across credentials and routes. Focus: timeline-driven investigation, token decomposition, and guided remediation steps to reduce time-to-signal for SREs and CS.
body:
Purpose and goals:
- Quick investigator surface for support/SRE/product when an API key or route experiences quota exhaustion, latency SLO misses, or abnormal token spikes.
- Combine high-cardinality telemetry (per-credential, per-route, per-model) into a single canvas where causality hypotheses can be built and validated.
- Provide actionable remediation: temporary quota bump, route fallback, model downgrade, or request inspection.

Desired users and flows (top-level):
1) Customer Success handles customer ticket: open canvas scoped to customer credentials and last 24h.
2) SRE on-call receives PagerDuty alert for "credential throttle surge": open canvas, pivot to token waterfall, apply rate policy simulator to test throttle mitigations.
3) Dev on customer side wants to understand which routes burned their quota: shareable canvas snapshot with per-route breakdown and example request samples.

Core elements of the canvas (wireframe-level descriptions):
- Top bar: scope selector (Credential dropdown, optional route filter, model variant), time window quick pills (1h, 6h, 24h, 7d), actions (snapshot, share link, export CSV).
- Left column: credential summary card. Shows active plan, committed quota, current usage %, last throttle timestamp, linked contacts (owner email), KMS tag. Minimal microcopy: "Credential health at a glance".
- Center: timeline heatmap + trace events. Heatmap rows are routes (group by normalized route id), columns are 5-min buckets. Overlaid icons: throttle events, quota policy changes, rollouts, and backend errors (5xx). Hover shows sample request and token breakdown.
- Right: deep inspection pane. Tabs: (1) Token waterfall, (2) Sample request gallery, (3) Policy simulator, (4) Alerts & actions.

Token waterfall (detailed):
- View shows stacked bars per interval: prompt tokens, completion tokens, embeddings units, inference-cache hits, replays/retries. Each bar expandable to show top N routes contributing. Secondary bars show cost estimate and latency percentile.
- Quick filters: show only function-calls, show only streaming responses, exclude cache hits.
- UX note: include small sparkline of unit-cost impact when toggling quantization or model downgrade.

Sample request gallery:
- List of representative requests that consumed the most tokens in the selected window. Columns: timestamp, route, token_count, model, webhook status, truncated request/response preview.
- Click to open request inspector: full headers, body, and reconstructed billing footprint with attribution to route/credential/route-tag.

Policy simulator (interactive):
- Lightweight controls: reduce per-request token cap, apply per-route throttle (n req/min), swap to a cheaper model variant. Simulator computes projected token usage and percent change in throttle events.
- Export recommended action as a patch to a policy object (format consistent with infra-spec).

Alerts & actions:
- One-click: temporary override (credit bump) UI with explanation of risks. Pre-filled options from product-mapped playbooks (e.g., "Allow +10% for 1h and notify owner").
- Create follow-up: open a linked ticket template to CS/Sales/Account manager with snapshot and suggested next steps.

Interaction modes and states to design for:
- Triage state: default, heavy-read (many events), degraded telemetry (gaps), and replay mode (step through timeline).
- Collaboration: comments pinned to a time bucket, @mentions, and threaded notes. Snapshots should be immutable and shareable.

Data needs and backend contract (notes for infra/observability):
- Required metrics per 1-min bucket: token_count by category (prompt/completion/embeddings), request_count, avg_latency_p50/p95, throttle_count, cache_hit_count, policy_changes, error_count.
- Sample request retention: raw request samples + synthetic anonymization for PII before storing in long-term logs.
- Indexing: ability to query by credential-id and route-id with low-latency for 24h windows.

Open UX questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- Do we default the canvas to credential scope or route scope? (CS workflows prefer credential-first; SRE prefers route-first). Proposal: default to credential scope, remember last-used scope per user.
- How much request detail do we surface inline vs behind a permission gate? Need product + security decision: masking policy for request bodies.
- Snapshot size: snapshots should omit raw full request bodies by default. Option to include them for enterprise-only exports.

Accessibility and microcopy notes:
- Use passive voice for incident notes: "Throttle applied at 14:22 UTC due to burst" (avoid placing blame).
- Color palette: heatmap should be colorblind-safe; provide pattern overlays for heavy bands.

Low-fidelity wireframe annotations (for designers):
- Timeline hover card: route label, bucket start time, top 3 contributing requests, button: "Open bucket inspector".
- Bucket inspector modal: waterfall chart at top, sample requests list below, action buttons at bottom (Apply override, Create ticket, Export CSV).

Backlog (candidate tickets, prioritized):
- P0: JIRA-13001 - Canvas backend index API: credential+route low-latency query (1min buckets).
- P0: JIRA-13005 - Token decomposition aggregation pipeline (prompt/completion/embeddings/cache).
- P1: JIRA-13120 - Policy simulator UI + server-side projection endpoint.
- P1: JIRA-13135 - Snapshot share links + access controls and expiry.
- P2: JIRA-13210 - Request sample anonymizer and retention policy implementation.
- P2: JIRA-13250 - Commenting/notes and clone snapshot feature.

Edge-case scenarios to test during design review:
- Burst from many small concurrent requests vs a single giant request: verify waterfall correctly attributes tokens.
- Route aliasing: multiple route names mapping to same backend handler — need normalization to avoid fragmentation.
- Multi-tenant routes: same route id used by multiple customers in dedicated deployments — ensure tenant isolation in the canvas.

Support playbook snippet (for CS use):
- Step 1: Open credential canvas scoped to customer. Check top 5 routes by token usage.
- Step 2: If throttle_count > 0 in last 1h, open Policy simulator and try a temporary 10% quota bump for 30m. Evaluate simulated impact.
- Step 3: If heavy requests linked to a particular route with function-calls, advise customer to enable prefix caching or reduce max_completed_tokens.
- Step 4: If repeated bursts, create a rollout plan to add a cheaper model variant for non-critical routes (document in snapshot).

Notes to engineering/design handoff:
- Provide example JSON shape for canvas API in Confluence page (linked in linked_artifacts). Keep response size < 1.5MB for 24h windows.
- UX request: include precomputed top-N heavy requests per bucket to avoid expensive live queries.
- Security: default to redacted request bodies unless enterprise flag is on.

Next steps and owners:
- Aisha: consolidate design sketches and schedule 1hr sync with infra (week of 2026-02-24).
- Marco: prototype timeline heatmap component (MVP: static fixtures) by 2026-03-10.
- Sofia: draft permission model and snapshot access controls by 2026-03-03.
- Daniel: confirm telemetry availability and retention with observability by 2026-02-28.

Quick sketches attached: "forensics-canvas-v1.png", "bucket-inspector-flow.pdf" (designer drop). (These are referenced assets; actual upload pending.)

Loose ideas for future phases (parking lot):
- Auto-suggested remediation: ML model that proposes the smallest action to lower throttle risk (e.g., cap or model-swap).
- Incident timeline playback: play through events with ability to step to the exact request causing spike.
- Cross-customer anomaly detection: surface customers with similar route profiles when troubleshooting platform-wide anomalies.

End of doc.
